arxiv-2105-04004.title: Low dimensional flow polytopes and their toric ideals Thanks: Partially supported by National Research, Development and Innovation Office, NKFIH K 119934, K 132002 and PD 121410.
arxiv-2105-04004.creator: M. Domokos and D. Joó
arxiv-2105-04004.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Domokos and D. Joó. The toric ideal of a d d -dimensional flow polytope has an initial ideal generated by square-free monomials of degree at most d d . The toric ideal of a flow polytope of dimension at most four has an initial ideal generated by square-free monomials of degree at most two, with the only exception of the four-dimensional Birkhoff polytope, whose toric ideal has an initial ideal generated by a square-free cubic monomial.

arxiv-2110-09724.title: Valley transport driven by dynamic lattice distortion
arxiv-2110-09724.creator: Yuya Ominato, Daigo Oue, Mamoru Matsuo
arxiv-2110-09724.description: Abstract Angular momentum conversion between mechanical rotation and the valley degree of freedom in 2D Dirac materials is investigated theoretically. Coupling between the valley and vorticity of dynamic lattice distortions is derived by applying the k ⋅ p k\cdot p method to 2D Dirac materials with an inertial effect. Lattice strain effects are also incorporated.

arxiv-2203-01150.title: Embedding K 3 , 3 K_{3,3} and K 5 K_{5} on the Double Torus
arxiv-2203-01150.creator: William L. Kocay
arxiv-2203-01150.description: Abstract The Kuratowski graphs K 3 , 3 K_{3,3} and K 5 K_{5} characterize planarity. Counting distinct 2-cell embeddings of these two graphs on orientable surfaces was previously done by using Burnside’s Lemma and their automorphism groups, without actually constructing the embeddings. We obtain all 2-cell embeddings of these graphs on the double torus, using a constructive approach.

arxiv-2510-25546.title: Model Reduction for Controlled Quantum Markov Dynamics
arxiv-2510-25546.creator: Tommaso Grigoletto, Lorenza Viola, Francesco Ticozzi
arxiv-2510-25546.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tommaso Grigoletto, Lorenza Viola, Francesco Ticozzi. We consider the problem of model reduction for Markovian quantum systems whose dynamics are described by a time-dependent Lindblad generator – notably, as arising in the presence of external control. Our approach, which builds upon Krylov operator subspaces and operator-algebraic techniques introduced for time-independent generators, returns a reduced model that reproduces exactly the evolution of observables of interest and is guaranteed to be in Lindblad form.
